stem_book: In the example involving e^(sin x) − e^(−sin x) − 4 = 0, which substitution is used to simplify the equation? (a) t = cos x (b) t = sin²x (c) t = e^(sin x) (d) t = tan x
reason: Manifest stem lost the exponents ("e (sin x)"); stem_book restores e^(sin x), e^(−sin x).
work: t = e^(sin x) ⇒ t − 1/t − 4 = 0 ⇒ t² − 4t − 1 = 0, a quadratic in t
